title: Grace-period credits, invoice holds, and SLA-offsets for security questionnaire remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Enterprise customers occasionally submit security questionnaires that reveal gaps requiring remediation (e.g., encryption config, audit log retention). While remediation work is agreed in contract SOWs, the immediate operational need is to provide predictable billing behavior during remediation: invoice holds, provisional credits, and SLA credit offsets. This ticket defines the PM requirements and edge-case flows for credits/holds/proration in these security-driven scenarios.

Goals:
- Define a playbook for placing invoices on temporary hold while remediation is in progress without producing surprise usage overages.
- Create a deterministic policy for issuing provisional credits (timeboxed), and how those credits interact with existing prepaid credits, trial credits, and reserved capacity commits.
- Specify how SLA uptime credits are applied / offset when remediation work is customer-triggered via security questionnaire findings.
- Ensure auditability: all holds, credits, and reversals must be logged with link back to the questionnaire ticket and signed approval.

Scope & non-goals:
- In scope: invoice holds up to 90 days for remediation where a customer has a signed remediation plan; provisional credit issuance up to 30 days; rules to prevent double-crediting with auto-proration and reserved capacity accounting; UI/Console affordances for Finance and CSMs.
- Out of scope: renegotiation of contract pricing or long-term refunds beyond established credit windows (those handled by Finance ops).

Key requirements:
1) Hold lifecycle: creation -> pending -> active -> release -> reconcile. Holds must be tied to a security_ticket_id and include remediation owner, estimated completion date, and approval artifact (signed SOW or email). Holds should not prevent metering collection (we still track usage) but should prevent automated invoice generation and payment collection.
2) Provisional credits: Finance can issue provisional credits with an expiration date. Provisional credits can be applied to future invoices or refunded if remediation fails; they must surface in billing exports and the console ledger.
3) Interaction with reserved capacity & prepay: If reserved capacity commits exist, credits must first apply to pay-as-you-go overages and then to future invoice amounts; committed capacity charges are not refundable unless Finance approves contract amendment.
4) Trial credits & promo overlaps: Trial credits should be consumed before provisional credits; system must prevent stacking of multiple promotional credits beyond configured policy.
5) SLA credits and offsets: For incidents or degradation discovered during security remediation where Redwood is responsible, SLA credits will be issued per the contract. If remediation is customer-driven, SLA credits may be limited or offset against provisional credits—policy must be explicit and auditable.
6) Audit trail & evidence: Each action (hold, credit issuance, reversal) needs a link to the security questionnaire PDF (Confluence or Drive), PR for remediation work, and approval by: CSM + Finance Ops + Security.

Trade-offs & decisions to make:
- Lenient vs conservative holds: Lenient holds reduce customer friction but increase Finance complexity and risk of revenue leakage. Recommend pilot with conservative 30-day provisional credit window and manual Finance approval.
- Manual vs automated flows: Automation reduces toil; however approvals (especially for >30 day holds or >$50k credits) should be manual initially.

Proposed UX surface: Console > Billing > Invoice Holds tab (CSM/Finance only) showing: security_ticket_id, customer contact, hold_creator, created_at, reason, estimated_end_date, provisional_credit_amount, approval_status, compliance artifacts link. Ability to export ledger rows and add comments.

Data & meter implications:
- Preserve full usage metering granularity (per-model, per-region) even while on hold. This ensures accurate post-remediation billing and avoids blind spots for audits.
- Add a hold_flag to billing export rows and SDW ingestion so downstream reports can filter or aggregate holds.

Compliance/Legal constraints:
- Some customers will require invoice holds to be referenced in their security questionnaire responses. Need legal-approved templated wording for the hold.
- Security review required for any automation that creates credits tied to security findings.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence: https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EB/pages/SEC-BILLING-HOLDS-Playbook (draft)
- Finance runbook (Google Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/fakepath/RemediationCredits
- Acceptance criteria doc: https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EB/pages/PM-51723-Acceptance
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.internal.redwood/billing-holds-proto

Acceptance criteria:
- Finance users can create/update/release holds in the console UI (auth gated).
- Holds prevent invoice generation for the hold window and create a hold_flag on billing exports.
- Provisional credits appear in customer ledger and are automatically consumed per policy.
- All actions require an approval artifact link and produce an audit log entry with user and timestamp.
- Pilot rollout to 5 enterprise customers with active security questionnaire remediations and Finance partner sign-off.
comments: 2026-02-11 - PM triage: scoped to pilot. Assigned to Liam Chen for engineering touchpoint and Sarah Morales (Finance) for ops runbook.
2026-02-16 - Eng sync: runtime metering team confirms adding 'hold_flag' to billing rows is low-risk. ETA: 2 sprints. (See PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/482)
2026-02-20 - Legal/Compliance feedback: need templated hold wording and retention policy for evidence artifacts. Added 'legal_review' label and looped in Priya Rao.
2026-02-25 - Finance ops: recommend provisional credit cap at $100k for manual approval threshold. Automated smaller credits (<$5k) could be self-serve for CSMs. Will add to runbook.
2026-03-01 - Design review: Console UX mockups ok. Added CSV export and bulk-release action for Finance users. Mockup link: https://figma.com/file/fakepath/billing-holds-proto

2026-03-05 - Decision: Pilot parameters approved: 30-day provisional credit window, manual approval required for credits >$10k, holds max 90 days with forced review at 30 and 60 days. Proceed to engineering backlog with Cycle 2026-W10 target for backend and limited UI.
2026-03-05 - Next steps: create ENG tickets for hold_flag export, provisional_credit ledger schema, and Console permission gating. PM to schedule pilot customers and prep Finance SOP.
